executive_summary.headline: The system works, but it carries serious risks that should be handled before any new feature.

points.text: Part of the system runs on .NET Framework 4.6.1, which its maker stopped fixing on 2022-04-26.
Passwords or keys are written inside the code.
An important part of the system uses ASP.NET Web Forms, a technology that is hard to hire for and cannot be upgraded in place.
An important part of the system uses WCF / ASMX web services, a technology that is hard to hire for and cannot be upgraded in place.
Part of the system runs on Bootstrap 4.3.1, which its maker stopped fixing on 2023-01-01.
Newtonsoft.Json 12.0.1, a library the system depends on, has publicly known security flaws.

executive_summary.recommendation: Recommended path: refactor — Modernize gradually behind the same interfaces (strangler pattern), starting with the hotspots. The system is built on .NET, .NET Framework, ASP.NET Core, ASP.NET MVC, ASP.NET Web Forms.

glossary.definition: The date after which the maker of a technology stops publishing fixes, including security fixes.
A security flaw that has been published (in OSV, CVE lists), with the affected versions.
A service that builds and tests the system automatically on every change.
Move as is / upgrade the platform underneath / restructure the code gradually.
A fact produced by a deterministic tool (a manifest, git, a scanner), not by an AI model.
A conclusion an AI model drew from the evidence; it was checked against the cited code, but should be confirmed.

faq.question: Is the system at risk today?
faq.answer: Yes. The first items in the risk list should be handled now.

faq.question: Can we keep it as it is?
faq.answer: Only for a short time: keeping it means accepting the risks above.

faq.question: How long would the recommended path take?
faq.answer: About 105–237 weeks for a team of 3, plus the first two roadmap phases. These are ranges from the size of the code and the findings, not a commitment.

faq.question: What should we do first?
faq.answer: Phase 0 of the roadmap: close exposed secrets and known vulnerabilities, and get builds running automatically.

faq.question: How sure are these findings?
faq.answer: All 17 findings are verified by tools (manifests, git history, scanners). Each one links to its evidence.
